title: Seychelles
capsule: The Seychelles archipelago of 115 islands in the western Indian Ocean became a British crown colony in 1903, separated from Mauritius administration, and achieved independence on 29 June 1976, the same year this dataset's attestation begins. France-Albert René seized power in a bloodless coup in June 1977 and governed as a single-party socialist state until political liberalization in 1991; he won subsequent multiparty elections and retired in 2004, succeeded by James Michel and then Danny Faure in 2016. The economy shifted from plantation agriculture (copra, cinnamon) to tourism and, after 2000, to offshore financial services; Seychelles has one of the highest GDPs per capita in Africa. The country is also notable as the primary world habitat of the Aldabra giant tortoise and the coco de mer palm.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Modern sovereign archipelago state; island boundaries are well-documented, though the scattered nature of 115 islands across a large ocean area creates a complex maritime boundary framework.
